subtopic: Responding to a natural disaster or accident
subtype: Approach: calling for help and giving clear information [Action]
passage: The bang came from the crossing outside our school gate, and then a scooter lay on its side and two people were on the road. Everyone started shouting. Karthik grabbed my arm, his phone screen black: “Bhai, you call, it's dead.” My hands were shaking, but I dialled the emergency number. I gave the name of the road, the tea stall next to the gate, two people hurt, a scooter and a small van, one of them not talking. The operator told me to stay on the line, and I did, standing on the pavement far from the traffic while the guard waved cars away. I didn't touch anyone. When the ambulance came, my voice still felt strange in my throat. I'm Manoj, and looking back, saying the place first and then how many were hurt made it easy for them to find us.

qa.q: How many people were hurt in the accident, according to Manoj?
qa.a: Two people were hurt, and one of them was not talking.

qa.q: How was Manoj feeling as he dialled the number?
qa.a: Manoj was nervous and shaken, since his hands were shaking, yet he still gave clear information.

qa.q: What could Manoj and the others do while waiting for the ambulance, and why?
qa.a: They could ask a teacher or another adult to come and stay with the hurt people, because trained help is on its way and Manoj should stay back from the traffic.

qa.q: How might Karthik feel about Manoj making the call?
qa.a: Karthik, whose phone was dead, probably feels relieved and grateful that Manoj stayed steady and gave clear details.

grounding: After a road accident near school, a student calls the emergency number, gives the place, number hurt and what happened, stays on the line and stays out of danger.

passage:
Teacher's note, Wednesday, incident near the school gate
At 3:15 a scooter and an autorickshaw collided at the corner outside our gate. I reached the gate a minute later, and by then Ramesh from Class Ten was already on the phone to the emergency number, standing on the footpath well back from the road.
I heard him clearly: “There's an accident at the corner of MG Road and Station Road, outside the main gate of Sunrise School. Two people are hurt. The scooter rider is on the ground and not getting up; the auto driver is sitting and bleeding from his arm. It happened one minute ago.” Then: “Yes, I'll stay on the line.”
He told his classmate Pooja to stop other students crowding the road, and he did not go near the traffic himself. He answered every question until the ambulance arrived, eleven minutes later.
I have told his parents and the principal how well he handled it.

qa.q: How many people did Ramesh say were hurt?
What might Ramesh have been feeling while on the phone?
qa.a: He was probably shaken and scared, yet focused enough to give clear details and stay calm on the line.

qa.q: Why did staying on the footpath matter?
qa.a: It kept Ramesh out of the traffic, so he didn't become one more person needing help while guiding the ambulance.

qa.q: What was Pooja's part in the scene?
qa.a: Pooja kept other students from crowding the road, which helped keep everyone safe while Ramesh made the call.

grounding: A teacher notes a student calling the emergency number after a road accident, giving the exact place, number hurt and what happened, and staying on the line from a safe spot.

passage:
Friday
Still shaky. After school, at the bus stop on Canal Road, a car hit a boy on a cycle. He was lying on the road holding his leg. Everyone just stared. Ojas started running toward him, into the traffic, and I grabbed his bag and pulled him back. “Cars!”
Then I called the emergency number. I made myself say it the way we learnt in the safety class: where, how many, what happened. “Bus stop on Canal Road, opposite the petrol pump. One boy hurt, he was on a cycle, hit by a car. He's awake, holding his leg.” The woman on the phone asked me to stay on the line and tell her if anything changed. I did, from the footpath.
The ambulance came in about ten minutes. A shopkeeper stood with the boy until it did.
I only realised afterwards how hard my heart was beating.
– Vijay

qa.q: Where exactly did Vijay say the accident was?
qa.a: Bus stop on Canal Road, opposite the petrol pump.

qa.q: What was Vijay feeling during and after the call?
qa.a: Vijay stayed focused during the call, but afterwards felt shaky, heart pounding, as the fear caught up.

qa.q: What else could Vijay have done while staying on the line?
qa.a: Ask an adult nearby, like the shopkeeper, to stay with the boy and keep people from crowding, while Vijay kept giving updates.

qa.q: How might Ojas see being pulled back?
qa.a: Ojas might be annoyed in the moment, but later glad to have been stopped from running into the traffic.
